files.title: File:Hexagonaria percarinata fossil coral (Petoskey Stone), Michigan.jpg
files.author: James St. John
files.caption:
Hexagonaria percarinata fossil coral (polished) (field of view ~3.6 cm across) - a “Petoskey Stone” from the Middle Devonian of Michigan, USA.


The “official state stone” of Michigan is the Petoskey Stone, the local name for rounded pebbles or cobbles of the fossil coral Hexagonaria percarinata Stumm, 1969.  Petoskey Stones have been weathered & eroded from fossiliferous limestones of the Traverse Group (Middle Devonian).  They are particularly common in the vicinity of Little Traverse Bay
